overview.text: The Eastern Ribbon Snake is a slender, harmless garter snake of eastern North America that is rarely found far from water.

identification.text: Dark brown with bright yellow stripes and a very slim body.

size.label: Adults
size.text: About 40 to 90 cm (16 to 35 in) long; females are usually thicker than males.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: South-eastern Canada (Nova Scotia, Quebec, Ontario) and the eastern United States from Maine to Florida and west to Louisiana and Michigan.

habitat.text: Along ponds, streams, swamps and wet woods or grassland. It uses shallow water to hunt and to escape. In winter it shelters underground, for example under rock piles.

diet.text: Hunts by sight: newts, salamanders, frogs, toads, tadpoles, small fish, spiders and earthworms - but never warm-blooded animals.

reproduction.text: Mates in spring and gives birth to 4 to 27 live young in summer. Young become adults after two or three years.

recognise.text: Very slim, dark brown with bright yellow stripes.
